transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee - Redwood (AE); Samira Khan - Redwood (SE); Priya Nair - Redwood (CSM); Dr. Maya Patel - Luminary (Head of Search); Ethan Brooks - Luminary (Data Eng); Lina Gomez - Luminary (ML Eng); Oliver Park - Luminary (Infra)

Summary (auto): Discovery call to understand Luminary's embedding/reranking requirements, integration architecture, security constraints. Discussed whether to use Redwood Hosted vector store + reranking or Redwood Dedicated/Private with self-managed vector DB (Milvus/Pinecone/Weaviate) for PHI workloads.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'll kick off quick, this is jordan from redwood, i'm the account lead, with me is samira who is our solutions engineer, priya from CSM also on to make sure we cover next steps
[00:07] Maya: thanks jordan, appreciate it. quick context: Luminary is building a clinical search experience for our provider portal, lots of semi-structured clinical notes, some structured fields. privacy is huge — some PHI will be present in queries and indexed docs.
[00:20] Jordan: understood. can you give us current stack and rough numbers? qps, dataset size, how you're doing search today?
[00:28] Ethan: yeah, today we run an internal elastic + BM25 hybrid for keyword; about 20M docs, avg doc length 800 tokens, we see peak query load ~300 qps, avg 80 qps. We're exploring embeddings + rerank to improve semantic recall.
[00:42] Lina: model wise we've prototyped with openai ada embeddings for research but cost and data residency are blockers. we also tried a 768-d clinical model locally.
[00:52] Samira: got it. two axes people typically care about: embedding dimensionality (512 vs 1024) which influences index size and perf, and throughput (QPS and concurrency) which impacts whether hosted vector DB with batching works or you need dedicated infra.
[01:04] Oliver: we also need private deployment. PHI means we can't have content leave our VPC unless contracts in place; any private option?
[01:10] Jordan: yes, redwood private is an option — customer-managed VPC with private control plane or on-prem package. we've done SOC2+KMS integrations with several healthcare customers. we'll share the security pack.
[01:20] Maya: curious about latency tradeoffs: if we do 1024-d embeddings and rerank top 100 candidates with a cross-encoder, what's the expected p95 latency on hosted vs dedicated?
[01:32] Samira: rough ballpark — a hosted API path with smart prefix caching and continuous batching can usually hold sub-200ms token latencies for generation, but for embeddings + vector search it depends on vector index. for a 1024-d dense index for 20M vectors, naive ANN can give sub-50ms per query on optimized hardware but at cost. with an external vector DB like pinecone or milvus, you have network hop; with dedicated we can co-locate smaller indexes on the same pool for lower latency. we typically recommend 512d for high qps if it's acceptable for quality — halves storage and speeds up ANN distance calculations.
[02:10] Ethan: question on hybrid search: we want BM25 + vector rerank. do you support hybrid out of box or do we have to orchestrate BM25 ourselves?
[02:18] Samira: Redwood supports combination patterns; for hosted we have re-rank primitives where you can send top-k from your BM25 and call reranker. we don't host BM25; usually customers run BM25 on their side (ES or solr) and call our reranker/embeddings for scoring. can also do prefix caching to reduce embedding compute if queries repeat.
[02:35] Lina: and how about vector DB integration? we currently plan to use Milvus but open to managed options. any connectors?
[02:42] Samira: we have adapters for common vector DBs — Milvus, Weaviate, Pinecone patterns — and we can integrate with your ingestion pipeline. if you go Redwood Dedicated or Private you can host the index with us or push to your DB and we call it — there are tradeoffs around egress and throughput.
[02:56] Oliver: network/egress is big for us. if we call a hosted index we'll have cross-tenant traffic; with dedicated we can request private peering. any notes on VPC peering latency?
[03:06] Samira: peering and private link reduces hop significantly; we've seen p95 drop by tens of ms vs public endpoints, depending on region. we'll need network team to confirm firewall rules and NAT.
[03:16] Maya: security questions: SSO, role-based access, audit logs, KMS — do you provide per-customer KMS integration and per-token audit?
[03:24] Jordan: yes, per-customer KMS/HSM integrations available in Private; audit logs and token-level billing in console. we'll attach SOC2 report and the architecture for KMS keys.
[03:33] Ethan: on cost, what's the typical unit economics? embeddings compute vs storage vs rerank cross-encoder cost? we need a rough model for budgeting.
[03:41] Samira: short answer: embedding compute is per-vector call, rerank with cross-encoders is heavier per-query. cost drivers: embedding dimensionality, QPS, index size (storage/replication), and whether you host the index with us (we bill storage & throughput) or you self-host (you pay infra). we can share a benchmark sheet with sample cost curves for 512/768/1024 dims.
[04:00] Lina: for accuracy, we've seen diminishing returns after 768 for clinical notes; curious if you have evaluation tooling to compare embedding spaces and rerank models.
[04:08] Samira: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regressions tied to prompt sets and evals; we can run A/Bs and track MRR/Recall@k.
[04:16] Jordan: okay, quick recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/security pack (jordan), samira will export benchmark template and sample throughput numbers for 512 vs 1024 dims, and we'll schedule infra deep-dive for VPC peering with oliver.
[04:29] Maya: sounds good. one more: competitor concerns — pinecone looked attractive but they have limited private deployment options; milvus is flexible but ops heavy. we may need managed but private.
[04:41] Jordan: totally, we'll include notes comparing managed vs self-hosted, and a suggested pilot path: start with hosted embeddings + our rerank on a redwood dedicated trial for a subset (non-PHI subset) to validate quality, then migrate to Private for PHI if the pilot meets criteria.
[04:56] Ethan: timeline wise we'd like pilot in Jan 2027, with decision by end of Q1.
[05:01] Jordan: great, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
